- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.67), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., 6.83, 10.07, 10.36) — cap forecast at 2x recent 7-day average if spike > 1.5x mean.  
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days show >1.5x mean deviation, apply mean reversion: adjust forecast to 0.85×previous day’s forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 1.5x recent 7-day average, reduce forecast by 15–25% for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., 0.67, -0.67, 0.67), model tends to lag — forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend.  
- When sentiment is flat (0.00 or 0.33) for 3+ days, model overestimates — reduce forecast by 10–15% for next 5 days.
